title: Large personal Amiga/ST/CPC/DOS language and source-port discovery
summary: Personally screen 1065 candidate URLs and add 20 projects, with eight explicit non-promotion decisions.
notes: Root personally searched 24 GitHub query routes, screened 1065 unique URLs and inspected 28 pinned repository trees. Twenty additions and eight explicit non-promotions. Historical source preservation, native compatibility interpreters, partial format recovery and enhanced derivatives are distinguished from original fidelity, generic remakes and CPU execution. No upstream game, compiler, installer, emulator, BBS or network service was executed.

sources.reason: Enhanced derivative of the TFX 2.05 reconstruction, with original-address-backed aircraft motion routines inspected. Higher resolution, configurable views and arming changes are explicit departures.
Enhanced fork of reconstructed Corncob 3D, with inspected continuous-time integration around original control laws. Native world/actor systems, not original executable dispatch.
Original-data animation, collision and encounter systems plus IDA extraction scripts. Inspected typed encounter components and original PIV/terrain readers, rather than a generic CPU runtime.
Reads IFF WORD and WOWO chunk streams, reconstructs paragraph/run formatting and emits DOCX/text. Inspected separate WTXT paragraph and older TEXT visual-line handling.
Reimplements Soft-Logik 1992 HotLinks public SDK ABI and edition publication protocol. Inspected actual LVO implementations and shared catalog management.
C++ rewrite of jAMOS with AMAL instruction interpreter/compiler and original ABK bank support. Inspected move interpolation, labels, pause and autotest language semantics.
Native PCBoard 15.4 command, display and PPE/PPL compatibility system. Inspected array-decay semantics and structured PPE VM, with original-source and DOSBox oracle methodology documented.
Ports Scott Miller original adventure source to Free Pascal, preserving parser, command logic, objects and room files. Inspected substantive command implementation.
Ports original Scott Miller adventure source, preserving parser state, inventory/event sets and save records. Inspected NOVA main program structures.

Semester Port+ conversion retains original Turbo Pascal alongside Python gameplay and mapped original tile identities. Reviewed Cycle-3 final product rather than counting historical cycles as separate games.
Original author preserves 1996 Borland Pascal game and later SDL/Free Pascal conversion. Inspected actual two-player progression and bonus-level logic.
JavaScript rewriting based on CSBWin and original Atari ST dungeon data. Inspected map header, object count, start-position and level decoding in substantial dungeon source.
xRick-derived native TI-99 port, primarily using Atari ST-derived rules/assets. Inspected fixed-point movement, collision flags and original address annotations.
Unified three-episode source-derived engine plus reconstructed original launcher and data tooling. Inspected actor movement from original C and native-port structure.
Original author recovered asset archives, textures, animation and localization pipeline after losing Turbo Pascal gameplay source. Inspected XOR directory decoding and archive repacking.
Portable DAAD interpreter/compiler and graphics/database tools; inspected machine-specific ink maps and command interpreter source. Original game-language execution, not original CPU emulation.
IDA-backed recovery of DOS game commands with original data offsets, officer/province structures and CGA rendering. Inspected award/loyalty calculation rather than a generic x86 dispatcher.
Reworks recovered VIGASOCO game logic into lower-overhead structures. Inspected structured Abbot state/routine tables rather than CPU instruction interpretation.
Abbey/VIGASOCO semantic game logic compiled to 68008 with handwritten 68000 renderer, QDOS integration and save/audio adaptations. Inspected original-derived character state logic.
Reimplements GEM calls through client library and display daemon, with native desktop and resource parser. Inspected big-endian RSC objects, icons and tree loading.
Fork of tracked rm3g25/dark-planet-win; no separate recovery lineage established.
Fork of tracked NancySadkov/devroomm; same VROOMM overlay-manager source recovery, not another project.
Fork of tracked thedragonheir/re-zeliard; partial town reconstruction already represented upstream.
Preserves original Ron Davis release, with missing compression, audio and launcher code. Existing joncloud/got tracks the rebuild lineage; no independent restoration demonstrated in this mirror.
Pinned tree contains only README.md despite extensive implementation and compatibility claims. No source available here to substantiate application recovery.
README says maps and notes only; inspected current place is generic framework scaffolding, not recovered Ultima Underworld engine behavior.
Playable-style JavaScript recreation with custom movement constants, but no original code, data-format analysis or documented recovery method established by inspected README/player source.

Tribute reconstructed visually from play, with only one of three original modes and changed SVG presentation. Original algorithm/data recovery not established; not classified as reverse-engineered source.

decisions.reason: Ports original Scott Miller adventure source, preserving parser state, inventory/event sets and save records. Inspected NOVA main program structures.

decisions.reason: xRick-derived native TI-99 port, primarily using Atari ST-derived rules/assets. Inspected fixed-point movement, collision flags and original address annotations.

decisions.reason: Portable DAAD interpreter/compiler and graphics/database tools; inspected machine-specific ink maps and command interpreter source. Original game-language execution, not original CPU emulation.

decisions.reason: IDA-backed recovery of DOS game commands with original data offsets, officer/province structures and CGA rendering. Inspected award/loyalty calculation rather than a generic x86 dispatcher.

decisions.title: La Abadia del Crimen — VIGASOCO-derived native engine
decisions.reason: Reworks recovered VIGASOCO game logic into lower-overhead structures. Inspected structured Abbot state/routine tables rather than CPU instruction interpretation.

decisions.reason: Abbey/VIGASOCO semantic game logic compiled to 68008 with handwritten 68000 renderer, QDOS integration and save/audio adaptations. Inspected original-derived character state logic.

decisions.title: QGem — GEM API and resource compatibility reconstruction
decisions.reason: Reimplements GEM calls through client library and display daemon, with native desktop and resource parser. Inspected big-endian RSC objects, icons and tree loading.
